analysis.title: US Economic Perspectives: FOMC minutes: "almost all" see further hikes
key_insights: The October 27-28 FOMC minutes show the committee held rates steady, but "almost all" participants judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate, broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections.
"Some" participants favored a 0.25 pp hike at the October meeting. UBS thinks this is more than just the dissents from Hammack and Cook. "Most" supported holding the range.

"A couple" of participants said an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration in December. "Some" said market expectations for a December hike matched their own view of the right path.
Participants who supported the pause cited the need to assess AI-related investment demand durability, financing conditions, transmission of the September hike, and geopolitical developments.

Inflation concern has broadened. "Most" saw broad-based price pressures, and "many" saw AI-related demand straining supply and raising consumer goods prices, up from "some" in September. "Many" called the AI buildout a material source of inflation risk.

"Several" judged price pressures were increasingly extending beyond industries directly affected by data center construction. "A number" pointed to elevated market-based core non-housing services inflation. "The vast majority" saw upside risks to the inflation outlook.

Medium- and longer-term inflation expectations were judged anchored near 2%, but "a few" noted shorter-term measures had risen. Staff expressed increasing concern about longer-run expectations becoming unanchored.

Activity is described as expanding at a "strong" pace, upgraded from "solid" in September. Upward revisions to the national accounts suggest consumers have more savings, and elevated household wealth supports spending.

The labor market was seen as stable near maximum employment despite a soft payroll print a few weeks earlier. "Many" saw tightening, "some" noted low dynamism, and "most" judged wage growth consistent with 2% inflation.

Financial conditions tightened since September according to "a majority", and "many" said lower AI-related equity valuations could temper investment. "Several" still saw conditions as supportive of growth. "Most" flagged rapidly rising AI-related debt and hedge fund leverage as channels that could amplify stress.

Daly said "the bias for change is up" but declined to give guidance on the extent or timing of hikes given elevated uncertainty. Waller said a 0.25 pp hike in December with clear guidance for another in January is similar to the 0.50 pp hike he had suggested for December.
UBS expects the FOMC to deliver 0.25 pp hikes at the December and January meetings.
